records.metadata: Where are the Sun and Earth? Vertical axis: Elevation above local horizontal (°) Azimuth (° clockwise from north) on the horizontal axis. Elevation above local horizontal (°) on the vertical axis. North 0°, east 90°, south 180°, west 270°. Elevation 0° is the local horizontal, perpendicular to the site's reference-sphere radius. Sun is filled amber; Earth is a blue ring. The smooth-sphere horizon is 0°. A body is blocked when its direction falls below the terrain in that compass direction. Part of the Sun may still clear the rim when its centre does not. Tracks revisit directions at different times; they are not simultaneous. Native horizon spacing: 90°; observer height: 2 m. Horizon borrowed from the nearest precomputed cell; not measured at this coordinate. Each track readout identifies its own hourly stay sample; nearest directions need not be from the same time. Elevation over the surface stay Vertical axis: Elevation above local horizontal (°) Time (UTC) on the horizontal axis. Elevation above local horizontal (°) on the vertical axis. UTC dates and hours, not elapsed flight seconds. Elevation 0° is the local horizontal. Compare each body's centre direction with its terrain horizon and the smooth-sphere 0° line. Sun is filled amber; Earth is a blue ring. When the terrain line rises above a body's centre, the centre is hidden. The Sun's finite disk can remain partly visible; Earth communication uses its centre plus the antenna mask, not this chart alone.
